title: Emerald Bank - POC scoping: workload & traffic modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization for Redwood POC. Customer wants a 6-week pilot to validate latency and cost targets for an internal summarization + routing microservice. Key success criteria: p95 generation latency < 800ms for typical requests, stable throughput for 50 QPS steady-state, and SAML + KMS integrations validated. Next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan, security docs, and draft pilot runbook.

transcript:
Header: 2026-03-27 15:00 PT | Duration: 56m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Reyes (Emerald - Head of ML), Liam O'Sullivan (Emerald - Platform Eng), Priyanka Singh (Emerald - Security)

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to scope the POC today. quick agenda, workload profiling, success criteria, timeline, and next steps. Priya and I will lead the technical bits.
[00:35] Marta: Thanks Jared. high level we want to validate using Redwood for our internal doc summarization + routing service. main concerns are latency for user-facing flows and predictable cost. we'll also need SAML and KMS for the pilot.
[01:10] Priya: great, can you share current traffic numbers? qps, concurrency, request sizes? even ballpark helps.
[01:25] Marta: yeah so production currently peaks around 120 qps during morning batch, sustained is more like 40 qps. concurrency per instance is roughly 10-15 for the API workers. requests vary, about 60% short (~<128 tokens in input), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512). outputs are typically longer, avg around 220 tokens, with 70% under 256, 25% between 256-1k, small percent over 1k for long transcripts.
[02:05] Liam: to add, our worker timeout is 10s, so we need p95 well under that. we'd like p95 generation latency under 800ms if possible for the short/medium requests, longer ones can be asynchronous.
[02:35] Priya: ok that's helpful. for the POC we usually model a representative QPS profile: baseline 50 qps sustained with 2x burst to 120qps. do you expect traffic to be spiky? any diurnal patterns?
[03:00] Marta: spikes are predictable around 9-11am and 5-6pm. bursts from batch ingestion can hit up to 120 qps for 5-10 minutes.
[03:18] Jared: good, so pilot target we proposed: sustain 50 qps with ability to handle 120 qps short bursts, p95 latency <800ms for short/medium, monitor kv cache hit rate, and keep cost estimates per 1M tokens. does that align?
[03:34] Priya: yes and we'll ask for sample traces from you to run the exact token distribution during benchmarking.
[03:48] Priyanka: on the security side we need SAML SSO, RBAC for service accounts, and KMS integration for encryption at rest. also audit logs retention of 90 days for the pilot.
[04:05] Jared: Redwood supports SAML and KMS; we'll include our enterprise checklist. for the POC we can run in a private VPC or on Redwood dedicated depending on your preference and compliance needs. which do you think you want to start with?
[04:30] Liam: initially we'd like to try hosted with VPC peering if possible, if that doesn't meet our compliance we'll move to dedicated or private.
[04:45] Priya: ok we'll size both options in the spreadsheet. back to workload modeling: some clarifying q's — what's your avg tokens per request end-to-end (input+output)?
[05:00] Marta: rough avg input 160 tokens, output 220 tokens so ~380 tokens per request.
[05:12] Priya: great. with 50 qps that's about ~19k tokens/sec, peak bursts 120 qps ~45k tokens/sec. that's useful for GPU throughput estimates.
[05:30] Jared: and do you have any strict latency SLOs for tail? p99?
[05:40] Liam: p99 is nice to have but not blocking; p95 is the one that'll make product happy.
[05:50] Priya: noted. architecture wise, are you considering caching of prefixes or reranking? that impacts KV cache hit rates and effective token yield.
[06:05] Marta: we have some prefix caching for repeated system prompts, maybe 25-30% reuse, but not consistent.
[06:18] Priya: ok we'll model a cache hit rate of 20-30% in the benchmark to reflect that.
[06:28] Jared: let's talk about the benchmark plan — we typically run three phases: 1) synthetic single-instance latency profile with representative prompts, 2) scaled throughput test with synthetic load reproducing token distribution and concurrency, 3) production trace replay to validate end-to-end behavior. we'll provide load scripts and a spreadsheet to capture results.
[06:50] Marta: sounds good. for phase 3 we'll need to anonymize logs but we can provide token lengths and timestamps.
[07:02] Priya: excellent. any constraints on model family? are you flexible or locked to a specific model?
[07:12] Marta: we'd prefer an open model for cost reasons, but quality matters. top candidates are Llama2 family variants or Red-- Redwood mentioned faster Llama derivatives during product brief.
[07:30] Jared: right we have a couple of verified variants in our catalog. for the POC we'll pick a 13B quantized variant and also test a 70B quantized variant to show the tradeoffs in latency and cost.
[07:45] Priya: in terms of hardware, we'll propose two configs: dedicated A100-like GPU farm for low latency p95, and cheaper T4/8-bit quantized nodes for cost-optimized throughput.
[08:00] Liam: can you give a ballpark of instances needed for 50 qps based on your internal perf numbers?
[08:10] Priya: ballpark — for 13B quantized on Ampere-like instance we often see ~15-25 qps per GPU depending on sequence lengths and KV cache. with 380 tokens/request avg and 50 qps, rough estimate is 2-3 GPUs with batching and cache, plus safety margin. we'll quantify precisely in the sizing sheet.
[08:35] Jared: and for burst capacity to 120 qps we can either burst with autoscale pool or have pre-warmed spare capacity in dedicated. that's a policy decision.
[08:50] Marta: pre-warmed capacity is preferable to avoid cold-start spikes.
[08:56] Priya: noted. we'll include a recommended config that keeps one spare GPU headroom for bursts.
[09:05] Priya: about metrics we'd collect during the POC: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, error rate, and cost per 1M tokens.
[09:22] Marta: can you show an example results dashboard?
[09:28] Jared: yes we'll attach sample dashboards and per-route cost breakdown.
[09:34] Liam: for integration timeline how long to get a private VPC or dedicated tenant up for the pilot?
[09:42] Jared: typically 2-3 weeks for dedicated onboarding, private VPC slightly faster if it's hosted with peering — depends on networking approvals. for hosted + VPC peering we can often do it in ~10 business days.
[10:00] Priya: ops note — we'll need to validate KMS and SAML before we start heavy benchmarking; those are blockers for full data ingestion.
[10:12] Priyanka: yes and compliance will need the governance doc and SOC2 evidence.
[10:20] Jared: we'll attach our security pack and SOC2 report.
[10:26] Marta: great. on success criteria again, to be explicit: 1) p95 latency < 800ms for 60% of requests (the short ones), 2) sustain 50 qps with no more than 5% error rate for 2 hours, 3) cost per million tokens within the threshold we'll agree on after initial sizing.
[10:48] Priya: we'll add those to the runbook as pass/fail checks.
[10:54] Liam: what about fallbacks if the primary model is unavailable? can Redwood route to a cheaper model automatically?
[11:00] Jared: yes routing policies can fall back to compatible model variants or to a smaller quantized model; we'll demo automatic fallback and circuit-breaker behavior in the POC.
[11:12] Marta: ok would like to see how fallbacks impact output quality.
[11:18] Priya: we'll include quality checks using a held-out eval prompt set to measure regression when falling back.
[11:28] Jared: we'll need a small set of evaluation prompts from you for that.
[11:34] Marta: we'll prepare ~200 prompts representing common user queries.
[11:38] Priya: perfect. timeline — propose a 6-week POC: week 0 (setup & security), week 1 (single-instance latency tuning), week 2 (scaled throughput), week 3 (production trace replay), week 4 (quality/regression & fallbacks), week 5 (reporting & decision).
[11:58] Liam: that fits our schedule; we want a go/no-go by week 6.
[12:06] Priya: okay action items as we discussed, and we'll send the benchmark plan today.
[12:12] Jared: anything else?
[12:18] Priyanka: one more item — data retention on logs, can you confirm retention windows and redaction options?
[12:25] Jared: yes we'll include that in the security pack and outline options for redaction and short retention for the POC.
[12:34] Marta: perfect. thanks everyone.
[12:40] Jared: recap — we will: share benchmark plan & scripts, sizing spreadsheet, security docs; Emerald will share sample traces and eval prompts; schedule kickoff for week of 2026-04-06.
[12:56] Marta: thanks.
[13:00] End recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words and mis-heard product names (e.g., "Redwood dedicate" for Dedicated) may appear. Some terms may be slightly garbled (KV cache -> KV cash) in auto-transcript.
